We Are All Trying Here

모두가 자신의 무가치함과 싸우고 있다 (Moduga Jasinui Mugachihamgwa Ssaugo Ittda)

K-Drama · Series · South Korea · 2026

⭐⭐⭐☆☆100/10

Overview

The series follows the "Group of Eight," a group of filmmaker friends who met through their university film club. While most of them have built successful careers, Hwang Dong-man is the only one who still hasn't made his directorial debut after 20 years. As the characters struggle with failure, jealousy, insecurity, grief, family problems, and their own sense of worthlessness, they gradually learn that adulthood is not about having everything figured out — it is about continuing to try.

My Review

I'm not really into this type of drama. At first, after watching only two episodes, I thought it wasn't worth my time. But I still finished it, and I'm really glad I did. The main reason I didn't like it at first was Dong-man. He was SO talkative and his sharp tongue really irritated me. But after finishing the series, I finally understood what it was trying to say. It's about the life of an adult. I really liked the characters — Dong-man, Eun-ah, Gi-ran, Jun-hwan, Gyeong-se, Young-soo, Jin-man, Hye-jin, Choi, and Jeong-hee. Each of them had their own struggles, and I became deeply moved by the circumstances some of them went through. Dong-man spent 20 years trying to make his debut while constantly receiving criticism because of his personality and sharp way of speaking. Despite all that, he never completely gave up. Eun-ah's story especially made me feel sorry for her. Her parents abandoned her, particularly her mother, and the circumstances surrounding her life explained a lot about her self-destructive behavior. The moments when she experienced nosebleeds while dealing with emotional pain also made me feel terrible for her. Jin-man also broke my heart. Losing his daughter Yeong-sil seemed to take away his passion for poetry. He stopped writing for around ten years, and I felt like he wasn't just mourning his daughter — he had also lost a part of himself. I also felt sorry for Gi-ran, especially when she thought the male actor she worked with genuinely liked her, only to find out that he considered it nothing more than acting. Her circumstances as Jeong-hee's stepdaughter made her life even more complicated. I really liked the ending. Gyeong-se and Dong-man became close again like they used to be, Dong-man finally achieved his directorial debut and became a successful director, and Jin-man finally had a lead about his daughter Yeong-sil. As teenagers, we also experience pain, frustration, anxiety, struggles, and sometimes feelings that seem impossible to handle. But watching this series made me realize that being an adult is a completely different level of struggle. We really are all trying here.

Favorite Scene/Part

• Finally understanding Dong-man. • Dong-man finally getting his directorial debut. • Dong-man and Gyeong-se becoming close again. • Jin-man finally receiving a lead about Yeong-sil. • Eun-ah's story and the painful circumstances behind her behavior. • Seeing how every character was struggling with their own version of worthlessness.

Favorite Quote/Lines

“Instead of holding onto what won’t work out and getting jealous of other people’s success, start living more constructively and productively from now on.”
